title: U.S. House · Georgia's 14th District
area: Northwest Georgia, including Rome, Dalton, and Cartersville.

context.text: Former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene (R) withdrew from the Republican primary for this seat and left Congress in early 2026; a special election was held to fill the vacancy. Clayton Fuller (R) won the special general runoff election on April 7, 2026 and took office on April 14, 2026. He then won the May 19, 2026 regular Republican primary and is the incumbent on the November ballot.
Cook Political Report rates the November general election Solid Republican; Decision Desk, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball also rate it Safe/Solid Republican.

candidates.name: Clayton Fuller
candidates.ballotNote: Won the special general runoff election on April 7, 2026, then won the May 19, 2026 regular Republican primary

summary.text: Clayton Fuller is a U.S. Air Force veteran, former prosecutor, and former White House Fellow who won the special election to succeed Marjorie Taylor Greene in April 2026. He holds degrees from Emory University, Cornell University, and Southern Methodist University's law school.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in English from Emory University (2004), a Master of Public Administration from Cornell University (2006), and a J.D. from Southern Methodist University's Dedman School of Law (2009); later earned a master's degree in military arts and sciences from the Air Command and Staff College (2020).
Has served in the U.S. Air Force since 2009; career experience includes serving as a staff judge advocate and as a district attorney with the Lookout Mountain Judicial Circuit in Georgia.
Served as a White House Fellow, working in counter-terrorism between the White House and the Pentagon.
Won the special general election runoff for Georgia's 14th District on April 7, 2026, defeating Shawn Harris, and took office on April 14, 2026.

priorities.text: In a 2020 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response, described himself as a "Christian Conservative who will defend the unborn, support the 2nd Amendment, and fight illegal immigration."
Said he is "passionate about bringing prosperity and growth to small towns in North Georgia" and about reducing the national debt.

positions.summary: Describes himself as a Christian conservative who will "defend the unborn."

record.text: Won the special general election runoff for Georgia's 14th Congressional District, 55.9% to 44.1%, on April 7, 2026, and took the oath of office on April 14, 2026.

candidates.name: Shawn Harris
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Democratic primary; also the Democratic nominee in the March–April 2026 special election for this seat

summary.text: Shawn Harris is a U.S. Marine Corps and Army veteran and Democratic nominee who ran against Marjorie Taylor Greene in 2024 and against Clayton Fuller in both the 2026 special election and the regular general election.

background.text: Born in Blakely, Georgia; served in the U.S. Marine Corps and the U.S. Army.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Tuskegee University and a graduate degree from the Army War College.
Was the Democratic nominee against incumbent Marjorie Taylor Greene in the 2024 general election, losing 64.4% to 35.6%.
Ran in the 2026 special election for the vacant seat, finishing first in the March 10 special general election and losing the April 7 runoff to Clayton Fuller, 55.9% to 44.1%.

summary.text: Andrew Underwood is a Libertarian Party candidate from Chickamauga, Georgia, whose campaign focuses on inflation, tariffs, and requiring members of Congress to read legislation before voting on it.

background.text: Majored in physics in college; work experience has mainly been in manufacturing and quality control.

priorities.text: Says affordability has become a major issue due to inflation, tariffs, and excessive regulation, and pledges to "work to remove these problems."
Says no legislator should vote for a bill without reading it in full, and that he would vote no on anything he could not read in time.
Says the national debt, which he notes has exceeded $38.6 trillion, is "out of control" and calls for balancing the federal budget.

positions.summary: Says "unnecessary and inconsistent tariffs" are hurting businesses and preventing them from planning for future expenses.

summary.text: Rob Ruszkowski is an independent candidate for Georgia's 14th Congressional District who also ran in the 2026 special election for this seat.

sources.title: Georgia's 14th Congressional District election, 2026 (Candidate Connection survey responses)

No campaign website, statements, or survey responses were found for Rob Ruszkowski beyond his candidacy in the special and regular elections; no additional public statements from Shawn Harris's 2026 campaign were located beyond his biographical page.
